items.title: SoftBank Group sinks into losses as its AI hopes falter | AP News
items.summary:
Tech

SECTIONS Artificial IntelligenceSocial Media  

TOP STORIES 
       Staff at the US center for AI safety are reporting to the White House, raising independence concerns
       Anthropic is rapidly accelerating AI development amid slowdown calls, outside research group says
       Milei pitches Patagonia for AI data centers as resistance grows in the US and Europe

   
Lifestyle

SECTIONS Food & RecipesGardeningFashionHomesTravelPets [...] — SoftBank Group sank into losses for the latest quarter, the Japanese technology company reported Tuesday, as worries about investments in artificial intelligence hurt its bottom line.

Tokyo-based SoftBank Group Corp. racked up a 1.1 trillion yen ($7 billion) loss for the three months through September, a reversal from the 2.5 trillion yen in profit the same period a year earlier. Quarterly sales rose 16% to 2.2 trillion yen from 1.9 trillion yen. [...] Analysts say the financial results for a company like SoftBank Group are difficult to predict as it invests in a variety of other companies, including OpenAI and Arm Holdings, whose fortunes tend to be volatile.

items.title: Military-made AI tool helped thwart World Cup bomb threat - Federal News Network
items.summary:
A military-made artificial intelligence tool helped law enforcement thwart a bomb threat at the FIFA World Cup in California this summer.

The previously undisclosed incident occurred June 18, when Switzerland faced Bosnia and Herzegovina at SoFi Stadium outside Los Angeles, Army Capt. Ryan Hetrick, who leads the Pentagon’s Generative AI Task Force, said Nov. 6 at an AI event in Washington. [...] Hetrick pointed to a recent visit to the 101st Airborne Division at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, where he built an AI tool that cut the time it takes to execute a particular cyber operations workflow from 100 hours to 15. That tool is now available to all cyber officers across the department, he said.

“We don’t do policy shops. We don’t do PowerPoints. We go to the edge and build with the warfighter,” he said. “You can’t be building agents from the Pentagon.” [...] He urged others across the military to adopt his hands-on approach to AI integration, encouraging troops to partner with AI experts to learn cutting-edge techniques and to tap innovative service members as in-house AI gurus who can spread that knowledge further.

        Sign up for our daily newsletter so you never miss a beat on all things federal

items.title: Accurate medical advice from AI can still be dangerous | STAT
items.summary: Artificial intelligence is delivering health guidance at an unprecedented scale. Every week, more than 300 million people ask ChatGPT health questions. Now, the federal government is moving AI deeper into medical care to communicate directly and autonomously with patients. Chris Klomp, the nominee for deputy secretary of Health and Human Services, has called AI in patient care the agency’s “holy grail” for improving the nation’s health. [...] In October, several states sued OpenAI, alleging that ChatGPT gives dangerous medical advice and misleads consumers about safety. OpenAI says it will continue to improve the model. [...] But both the lawsuits and the company’s response focus on blatantly harmful content, not accurate health advice that can still be unsafe. A draft federal bill that Anthropic, the maker of Claude, has circulated to lawmakers would let the government block an AI model if it could imminently kill or seriously injure more than 50 people.

items.title: We built Control Room, a central system to track model workloads across our research infrastructure and stop them quickl
items.summary:
We built Control Room, a central system to track model workloads across our research infrastructure and stop them quickly when safety or security concerns arise.

It connects every research inference workload, including agentic sampling for model training and evaluation, data processing, and more. This works together with our misalignment monitoring systems, and halts model output within 35 seconds of a decision to intervene to stop or pause a job.

Control Room is just one part of our holistic approach for safe frontier model training and deployment.

https://t.co/tc0lBqFdS5

items.summary:
We partnered with @fmf_org and its member firms on a new framework to help identify when bypassing an AI system's safeguards could enable serious cyber harm, and prioritize stronger protections.

"...This framework is an important step toward a common methodology for evaluating and comparing the severity of cyber jailbreaks, including the capabilities they unlock and how readily they can be used. Shared approaches like this can help the AI and security communities build a clearer evidence base and prioritize improvements to safeguards."  - OpenAI's Sasha Baker, Head of National Security Policy
